correctness.rationale: The proof reduces Haar two-point quotient distances to exact radial-area data of the Voronoi cell; differentiating yields angular exclusion H. Strict Voronoi facet feet create disjoint arcs with explicitly computed noncancelling sqrt onset, while previously active arcs remain Lipschitz even at vertex thresholds. Facet support distances with multiplicities are recovered and known planar obtuse-superbase reduction yields the entire Gram matrix up to integral basis changes. Eight independent numerical configurations and 105 numerical integration/threshold comparisons corroborate but are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The natural scalar two-point Haar distance law is proved to reconstruct all planar flat-torus shapes and scales, with exact singularity-based reconstruction through every four-/six-facet degeneracy. This inverse rigidity is not an arbitrary slice, simple moment, or parameter renaming; it gives the full isometry class of a compact Riemannian manifold from a one-dimensional geometric probability observable. No numerical stability or higher-dimensional generalization is claimed.
